resume: A neutral professional to help you reach agreements about the children together. Free information meeting, fees based on your income in an association approved by the Caf de La Réunion, agreement that can be approved by the judge.
aQuoiCaSert: Family mediation (médiation familiale) helps parents restore dialogue and build their own agreements: the child's residence, visiting and staying rights, child support, holidays. The mediator is independent and impartial: they decide nothing for you. The agreement can then be approved by the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF), which is called court approval (homologation), and then has the same force as a judgment. Mediation can take place before any court proceedings or during them.
quiEstConcerne: Parents who are separated or separating, married or not.
Grandparents, to maintain relations with their grandchildren.
Mediation is not possible in cases of violence by one parent against the other or against the child: in that case, call 3919 (listening line) or 17 (emergency).
aSavoir: The information meeting is free and without commitment.
Sessions usually last 1.5 to 2 hours. In out-of-court (voluntary) mediation, their number is often limited to 6.

The mandatory prior attempt at family mediation, trialed in particular at the tribunal judiciaire de Saint-Denis (the local court), ended on December 31, 2024: mediation is no longer a condition for applying to the judge, but the judge can still order you to meet a mediator.

With an association approved by the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office), the price of the sessions depends on your income. A private mediator sets their own fees; failing agreement, the costs are split in half.
The Caf de La Réunion funds approved family mediation associations: it can refer you to a service at the approved rate.
Court-ordered mediation: 5 months at most, renewable once for 3 months. The costs are split equally unless decided otherwise, and covered by the State if you have legal aid (aide juridictionnelle).
The judge can order the parents to meet a mediator. Refusing to attend can lead to a civil fine of up to €10,000.
Lists of mediators are published by each court of appeal, under "Partenaires de justice": for Réunion, the cour d'appel de Saint-Denis.
